editorial.headline: False Hair, Real Manufacturing Rules
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32906 covers the making of wigs, false beards, false eyelashes and similar products, nationally open to PMA but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32906 is a manufacturing code for the production of false-hair and similar appearance products. The slim record defines the activity as the making of wigs, false beards, false eyelashes, and other similar products. That makes the code about production, not retailing, salon services, beauty consulting, or distribution. Its centre of gravity is the factory or workshop activity: turning materials into finished false-hair products that can enter the market under this industrial classification.

The code is open across the full business-scale ladder recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration language, that means the activity is not confined to one size of Indonesian business in the record. A micro workshop, a small maker, a mid-sized manufacturer, or a large-scale producer can all sit inside the scale range shown for this activity, provided the registration itself follows the applicable OSS pathway for the chosen scale and location. The editorial point is simple: the activity scope is narrow, but the eligible business scales are broad.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture looks open. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership as 100%, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source. On the national data alone, a foreign-owned company can read this as a fully open manufacturing activity, not a capped one. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, so the national number should be stated plainly and not diluted with invented caveats.

Bali changes the conclusion. The record marks Bali as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. The reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026”. Read together with the moratorium rule in the record, Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest operational lede is this: KBLI 32906 may be nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreigner cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali today under the Bali-side rule recorded here.
